newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Assembly opens first session since election.
newsitem.headline: French Assembly opens first session since election.

text.p: France's National Assembly met on Thursday for the first time since the left swept to power last week and elected Socialist former prime minister Laurent Fabius as speaker.
The oldest member of the parliament, 85-year-old centrist Charles Ehrmann, presided over the opening session of the 577-member assembly elected in a two-stage vote on May 25 and June 1.

"I declare the...legislature open," Ehrmann told the assembly, which includes 62 women, up from 37 in the outgoing legislature. He was accompanied on the podium by the six youngest parliamentarians, starting with Victor Brial, 31.
Fabius, now 50, became France's youngest prime minister at the age of 37 in 1984. In the early 1990s he served a first stint as assembly speaker.

In Thursday's vote he needed a second ballot to nail down victory after initially failing to secure a majority. He succeeds conservative Philippe Seguin, who has now become floor leader of the Gaullist RPR party.

The election went to a second round because ecologists, angry over the Socialists' refusal to grant one of their members the chairmanship of the assembly's laws committee, put up their own candidate, Guy Hascoet.

Parties in the ousted centre-right coalition also presented rival candidates in a new sign of disarray after the snap election called by conservative President Jacques Chirac backfired on his allies and ended in their being consigned to opposition.
Newly-elected Communist deputy Patrice Carvalho attracted stares throughout the opening session by wearing blue overalls, saying they symbolised his working class roots.
But in deference to tradition, he wore a white shirt and tie along with the overalls.

"I decided to wear overalls because some of my fellow workers asked me to. They told me, 'We got you to the assembly, now you must show everyone that you come from the working world and intend to defend our interests'," Carvalho told reporters.
Carvalho, a 45-year-old mechanic who works at a French glassmaker's, was one of 38 Communists elected in last week's Socialist-led victory.
Deputy Alain Bocquet, leader of the Communist group in parliament, took credit for convincing Carvalho to don the white shirt and tie.
"Here all voters must be represented with dignity. If we had a championship swimmer in our group, I wonder what he would want to wear," Bocquet told reporters.

Former Socialist culture minister Jack Lang caused a sensation in the 1980s by turning up to the Assembly dressed in a so-called "Mao suit", a plain Chinese suit popularised by late chairman Mao Zedong.
